correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives beta(2u)=beta(u) when u is odd, beta(p^a)>=phi(p^a), and beta(u)<u for u>1. Equality beta(2u)=beta(2u+1) forces phi(m)/m<1/2 for m=2u+1; the n=2 case is separately false. For odd m with Omega(m)<=3, one or two distinct prime divisors give at least 8/15; three distinct require primes 3,5,r with r in {7,11,13}, as r>=17 yields 128/255>1/2. Thus m in {105,165,195}; n=m-1 must be 2 mod 4, eliminating 104 and 164. At n=194, beta(2*97)=96=beta(3*5*13). The argument holds without any bound on the odd cofactor u. Independent sieve checked all admissible n<60000 with only n=194; this is finite corroboration.

originality.rationale: The older Toth survey defines the identical multiplicative alternating divisor sum, poses the adjacent-equality problem, and records the value 194 as an example. That finite witness is prior, not novel. OEIS A206368 lists further equal neighbors but has no unbounded restriction theorem. The new statement excludes all other candidates with nu2(n)=1 and Omega(n+1)<=3, without requiring n/2 to be prime. This is not entailed by an earlier prime-only 2p classification or the list of examples, although the small-prime totient sieve is elementary; an unindexed equivalent classification remains possible.

value.rationale: The valuation-one layer is structurally natural because beta(2u)=beta(u). Three distinct odd prime factors are the first possible layer where phi(n+1)/(n+1)<1/2, so Omega(n+1)<=3 is a mathematically motivated sharp cutoff rather than an arbitrary large bound. Establishing exactly one solution in an unbounded entire congruence class advances an explicitly posed adjacent-equality problem; the novelty is the classification, not discovery of 194.
